# Results — Study 33 (Slingshot) on the real S&P 500

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Daily total-return panel of the **current
S&P 500** (467 names with ≥2500 days of history) via the shared `quantlab.universe` engine, 2010–2026.
The strategy is a **dollar-neutral cross-sectional reversal book**: each day, short the names that have
risen most relative to the cross-section over the trailing 5 days and long those that have fallen most,
gross exposure normalised to 1, rebalanced daily. Cost charged per unit of turnover. The offline core
proves the apparatus on a synthetic panel with idiosyncratic Ornstein-Uhlenbeck overshoot; this is the
measurement on the market. As-of **2026-06-10**; match the fingerprint below. **Caveat:** the panel is
today's index membership → survivorship bias; the reversal *sign* is robust, exact magnitudes are not.*

## The verdict, earned — Signal `REAL` · Tradability `MIRAGE` · Decayed since 2020? `CONFIRMED`

This is the deliberate counterpart to [Study 32 (Rip-Tide)](../../32-rip-tide/), and the contrast is the
whole point. The *same* "fade the recent move" idea that earned a gross Sharpe of **0.08 (≈ nothing)**
on deep futures earns a gross Sharpe of **0.70**, with clean **+0.73 skew**, on the cross-section of
single stocks. Short-term reversal is **`REAL`** — exactly where the liquidity-provision theory says it
should live (in single names, not in deep index futures). But it is a textbook **`MIRAGE`** to trade:
the book turns over **63% of its gross book every day**, so its **break-even cost is 3.31 bp** — and that
sits *inside* the realistic round-trip cost band for S&P names (≈2–10 bp once you add spread and impact),
while the premium itself concentrates in the *least* liquid names where costs are highest. Net of a
gentle 5 bp the Sharpe is already **−0.36**. And the edge has **`CONFIRMED` decayed**: net sub-period
Sharpe runs **−0.14 / −0.04 / −0.85**, worst in the 2020–2026 HFT era — the fade that statistical-arbitrage
desks lived on has been competed down, exactly as Khandani & Lo (2007) warned.

## Data stamp

- **Panel**: 467 S&P 500 names, 2010-01-05 → 2026-06-10, 4133 days, inputs fingerprint `c7175a6f4a03`
- **Caveat**: current-membership panel ⇒ survivorship bias (delisted names absent)

## The reversal book — real gross, gone net

| | Sharpe | CAGR | vol | max-DD | skew |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **reversal (gross, 0 bp)** | **0.70** | +5.1% | 7.4% | −20% | **+0.73** |
| reversal (net @5 bp) | −0.36 | −2.9% | 7.4% | −45% | +0.74 |
| reversal (net @10 bp) | −1.42 | −10.3% | 7.5% | −84% | +0.75 |

A market-neutral Sharpe of 0.70 with positive skew, gross of costs, is a **real** effect (it is *not*
0.08 like the futures version). But it is the rent for providing liquidity, collected one day at a time —
and net of any realistic cost it is gone.

## The cost wall — turnover is the whole story

| cost (bp/unit) | 0 | 2 | 5 | 10 | 20 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| net Sharpe | 0.702 | 0.278 | −0.358 | −1.416 | −3.525 |

Turnover is **0.63/day**, so the **break-even cost is 3.31 bp**. For the most liquid mega-caps that is
borderline; for the average and smaller S&P names — where the reversal signal is *strongest* — realistic
round-trip costs exceed it comfortably. The edge survives only where it is weakest. `MIRAGE`.

## The horizon — a knife-edge, not a plateau

Lookback sweep (net Sharpe @5 bp): 1-day **−2.38**, 3-day **−0.74**, 5-day **−0.36**, 10-day **−0.32**,
21-day **−0.19**. The 1-day bounce is pure microstructure (negative once you pay to trade it); even the
best-net horizon stays below zero. Gross, the signal *strengthens* with horizon, but so does the
competing momentum effect, and none of it clears costs.

## Decay — `CONFIRMED`

Net sub-period Sharpe: **2010–2015 −0.14**, **2015–2020 −0.04**, **2020–2026 −0.85**. The book is
net-negative throughout and *most* negative in the most recent, most-arbitraged window — direct evidence
the short-term reversal premium has been competed away as faster players entered (Khandani & Lo 2007).
The beat-7 "slow it down to escape costs" rescue ([`extension.md`](extension.md)) scrapes a net Sharpe
of just **+0.10** at a 21-day hold — within noise, not an investable edge.
